messages.subject: Image Portrait vs. Landscape
parts:
Hi all,

Simple question about image formatting.
Using Tutorial 2 as an example:
Is there a simple way to render the image as a Portrait or a Landscape (i.e. can we turn the image on its side)?

http://shiny.rstudio.com/tutorial/lesson2/

# ui.R

> shinyUI(fluidPage(
>  titlePanel("My Shiny App"),
>  sidebarLayout(
>    sidebarPanel(),
>    mainPanel(
>      img(src="bigorb.png", height = 400, width = 400)
>    )
>  )
> ))

Something along the lines of 

img(src="bigorb.png", heinght = 400, width = 400, orientation = "landscape")

Can't seem to find relevant information!
Cheers

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Image Portrait vs. Landscape
parts:
I'm not entirely sure what you mean by portrait vs landscape, it's not something that you commonly encounter when including images in webpages. Do you literally want to rotate the image 90 degrees? If so, that can be achieved with CSS. Take a look at the transform property http://www.w3schools.com/cssref/css3_pr_transform.asp

If you don't know how to use that information, read the css chapter in the shiny tutorial
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/css.html

messages.author: ab767e4427a481df
messages.subject: Re: Image Portrait vs. Landscape
parts:
Thanks Dean

Using CSS was always an option, but I was hoping for something simpler. The reason for the need in this case is that I am uploading a .png image that is appearing as landscape when I want it as portrait (i.e. the image is on its side).
I followed your suggestions and this works fine, so thanks for the advice. Posting for completion:

img(src="bigorb.png", height = 400, width = 400, style = "transform: rotate(90deg)")

Cheers

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Image Portrait vs. Landscape
parts:
If it's the same image that you're always showing and you always want to have it rotated, I'd suggest rotateing the actual image itself (using MS Paint or whatever program) and then using that image, instead of doing it using CSS.  But if you need to rotate an image in the browser, this solution is as simple as it gets. Thanks for sharing
